body:
Finding the right name for your business can be frustrating.

You want something short, catchy, memorable — and of course, with an available domain.

Luckily, there are a ton of AI-powered business name generators that can help you get there faster.

As a branding expert, I’ve tested and reviewed most of them myself — so in this article, I’ll walk you through the best business name generators in 2025, explaining what each one does well, where it falls short, and who it’s best for.

Let’s get into it.

1. Brand Namer App

Let me start with my own tool — BrandNamer.app — because I built it specifically to solve the frustrations I faced as a branding consultant.

You can generate an unlimited number of names, customize the naming style, adjust the length, blacklist certain words, and even upload a short brand description to guide the AI.

What makes it powerful is that it’s built for professionals — not just founders looking for quick ideas.

It also checks domain availability automatically, so you don’t have to waste time switching between tabs.

Pros

  • You get complete control — style, length, and filters that actually make sense.
  • Built-in domain check for instant feedback.
  • Designed by a branding expert (me!) who understands how names need to sound and feel right.

Cons

  • Still new, so you won’t find tons of reviews yet.
  • Doesn’t replace your creative judgment — it’s a smart assistant, not a magic wand.

Best for:

Designers, agencies, and entrepreneurs who take naming seriously and want high-quality ideas fast.

2. Shopify Business Name Generator

If you just want to get started quickly, Shopify’s free generator is a solid option.

You type in a word or two about your business, and it instantly gives you hundreds of suggestions.

It’s built into the Shopify ecosystem, so if you plan to sell online, this tool can take you straight from naming to launching a store.

Pros

  • 100% free and very easy to use.
  • Great if you’re planning to open an online store on Shopify.
  • Generates names almost instantly.

Cons

  • The results depend heavily on the keyword you provide — vague prompts lead to generic results.
  • Limited customization — you can’t filter by tone or length.
  • Skews towards eCommerce-style names.

Best for:

Entrepreneurs launching an online shop who want quick and simple naming ideas.

3. Namelix

Namelix is one of the most popular AI name generators out there — and for good reason.

It creates short, catchy, and brandable names using AI.

You can also choose your preferred style (modern, classic, invented, etc.) and adjust how creative you want it to be.

I’ve used it for client projects when I wanted a quick spark of inspiration — and while it’s not perfect, it often surfaces some great starting points.

Pros

  • Completely free to use.
  • Generates tons of short, catchy names quickly.
  • Learns your taste over time as you favorite certain names.

Cons

  • Some names feel repetitive or generic.
  • Doesn’t check trademarks or social handles.
  • You might have to sift through a lot of ideas before finding the right one.

Best for:

Startups or freelancers who need lots of ideas fast and don’t mind filtering.

4. Looka Business Name Generator

Looka is great if you want to go from name to brand identity quickly.
You can generate names, check domains, and even see logo previews — all in one place.

I like how it connects the dots between naming and visual branding, which is often where founders get stuck.

Pros

  • Combines naming, logo, and branding in one workflow.
  • Lets you filter by name style (compound, invented, descriptive, etc.).
  • You can instantly preview logos using your generated names.

Cons

  • The upsells can get a bit aggressive — many features are behind a paywall.
  • Some name suggestions feel more algorithmic than inspired.
  • It’s easy to get distracted designing logos before finalizing the name.

Best for:

Entrepreneurs who want a fast name-to-brand workflow and don’t mind paying for convenience.

5. Wix Business Name Generator

Wix’s name generator is another quick and simple option.

You enter a few keywords, pick your industry, and it gives you names along with available domains.

If you’re planning to build your website on Wix, this is a convenient place to start.

Pros

  • Simple and beginner-friendly.
  • Checks domains automatically.
  • Integrates perfectly with Wix’s website builder.

Cons

  • Limited control over style and length.
  • Names can feel generic or templated.
  • Better suited for small projects than full-scale brands.

Best for:

Small business owners who plan to use Wix and need a quick name + domain combo.

6. NameCheap Business Name Generator

If your main concern is finding a name with an available domain, this one’s for you.

The Namecheap generator focuses on helping you secure the perfect web address while generating brand-friendly ideas.

You can even set a domain budget range and see live prices — super handy if you’re working on multiple ideas.

Pros

  • Built-in domain pricing and availability.
  • Shows you what’s actually buyable.
  • Includes basic logo previews.

Cons

  • The creative side of naming is limited.
  • Prioritizes domain availability over originality.
  • Not ideal if you’re not ready to purchase a domain yet.

Best for:

Founders who want to secure a strong domain early in the naming process.

7. Squarespace Business Name Generator

Squarespace offers a clean, minimal tool where you can type a few keywords and explore naming styles like “playful” or “professional.”

It even gives short explanations behind each suggestion, which can help you understand why the AI came up with it.

Pros

  • Clean and intuitive interface.
  • Explains each name’s reasoning — surprisingly helpful.
  • Perfect if you’re already using Squarespace to build your site.

Cons

  • Limited customization options.
  • No trademark or social-handle check.
  • More focused on website setup than deep branding.

Best for:

Creatives and small businesses who just need a solid, simple name and website.

My Advice as a Branding Expert

No AI tool will name your business for you.

But they can definitely help you explore directions you might not have thought of on your own.

Here’s how I recommend using them:

  1. Start with clarity. Write down who you are, what you do, and how you want people to feel when they hear your name.
  2. Use multiple tools. Run the same prompt through two or three generators — each has its own strengths.
  3. Shortlist and refine. Don’t settle for the first name you like; refine it, test pronunciation, check availability, and visualize it on a logo.
  4. Think long-term. Choose a name that can grow with your brand, not one that limits you.

If you want a tool that gives you flexibility and branding logic — try my own BrandNamer.app.

It’s designed by a branding expert (me) to help you generate smart, strategic name ideas that actually sound like brands.
